subject: Northbridge: LLM usage boundaries, EU residency, and evidence request
messages:
From: Samantha King <samantha.king@northbridge.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Lewis <paul.lewis@northbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: LLM usage / residency questions before POC

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the overview this morning. As we're lining up procurement, two items are blockers for our security review and legal:

1) Training/Model Improvement: Northbridge needs a firm commitment that data sent to the API for the POC (customer support transcripts + metadata) will not be used to train or improve public models or other customer models. We understand you have options (no-train/opt-out) — please confirm the exact contractual language you can commit to and whether that applies to prompt/response pairs and derived embeddings.

2) EU data residency / transfers: Some of our data subjects are EU residents. Can Redwood guarantee that data will remain within EU regions for processing/storage, or provide the list of subprocessors and the transfer mechanisms (SCCs, Adequacy, etc.) you rely on? We need to understand cross-border flows for the DPA.

If you can send a short summary + supporting evidence (subprocessors list, SOC2 report excerpt, and a statement of the no-training commitment), we can re-start legal review.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our kickoff is scheduled for 11/15.

Samantha
Samantha King
Head of Security & Privacy
Northbridge Systems

--
Attachment: sample_poc_scope.pdf (pdf)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@northbridge.com>
Cc: Paul Lewis <paul.lewis@northbridge.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: LLM usage / residency questions before POC

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (legal) and Connor (security) so they can provide the exact language and evidence.

Quick answers up front:
- No-training: Redwood offers a contractual "no model improvement" commitment for customer PII/workload on our Dedicated and Private deployment options; for Hosted we have a documented opt-out workflow. We'll include explicit wording covering prompts, responses, and embeddings.
- EU residency: We can process and store data in EU regions for both Dedicated and Hosted (region-restricted) customers. For Hosted customers who require EU residency we default to our EU region; when transfers occur (rare), we rely on SCCs + standard contractual terms.

Next steps: Dev will follow up with proposed DPA excerpts and Connor will attach the latest subprocessors list and SOC2 pointer. If Northbridge prefers, we can also propose a short attestation letter for the POC scope.

I'll keep track of timing to make your 11/15 kickoff.

Thanks,
Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Aisha Rahman | aisha.rahman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@northbridge.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 10:27:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: LLM usage / residency questions before POC

Samantha — thanks for the note and the scope. I pulled together two things for you: a short proposed DPA excerpt with a no-model-improvement commitment tailored to the POC, and the current subprocessors list. Both are attached.

Summary (high level):
- No-model-improvement clause (proposed excerpt): "Redwood agrees that, with respect to Customer Data submitted under the Statement of Work for the Northbridge POC (dated 11/15/2027), Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve or train models that are used to serve other customers or public models. This includes prompt/response pairs, embeddings, or any derived features. Redwood may process Customer Data for the sole purpose of providing the Services and maintaining system health and security, subject to the confidentiality and data minimization provisions of the DPA."

- Scope & duration: The commitment applies to data submitted during the POC and for 12 months after ingestion unless otherwise agreed. If Northbridge opts for Dedicated or Private deployment, we can extend a perpetual no-train commit for the tenant environment; we can discuss contractual language.

- Subprocessors & transfers: Attached is redwood_subprocessors_list_v2.pdf which lists our EU-region processors and the controls they have in place. Where data is processed outside the EU, we rely on SCCs. For customers who require stricter controls, we offer Private deployments with VPC and on-prem options to eliminate cross-border transfers.

- Evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report excerpts, current penetration test summary, and an attestation letter that covers the POC scope. SOC2 and pen test full reports require an NDA; we can share redacted excerpts and an executive summary right away.

Attachments: proposed_dpa_excerpt_NB-2027-014.docx (contains the redlined clause and alternatives); redwood_subprocessors_list_v2.pdf

If the wording above looks acceptable in principle, Laura can coordinate the attestation/deliverable timeline and Aisha can confirm the procurement path.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Samantha King <samantha.king@northbridge.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Lewis <paul.lewis@northbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 15:46:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: LLM usage / residency questions before POC

Dev / Aisha — this is very helpful, thank you. A few quick asks to keep legal moving:

- Please provide the proposed_dpa_excerpt as a clean text snippet we can drop into our DPA review doc (we have the docx you attached, but legal prefers an inline snippet for quick review).
- Could you confirm whether the 12-month post-ingestion timeframe is negotiable for the POC? Our legal lead prefers a 24-month observation window before anything could be used for improvement, even if that is time-limited.
- For the subprocessors list: please include the country of each subprocessor and whether that processor has access to raw prompt/response content or only metadata/metrics.

On evidence: we can proceed with redacted SOC2 excerpts and the attestation letter you mentioned. Paul and I will sign an NDA if needed to receive more sensitive artifacts.

If you can get the snippet and the updated subprocessors table by COB Fri 11/12, we can keep the 11/15 kickoff. Otherwise we may need to push the start by a week.

Samantha

--
